text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prince Kiril, son of Bulgaria's exiled king Simeon II arrived on Tuesday in Sofia to advise President Petar Stoyanov on stabilising the economy.
-- The state Bulgarian Telecommunication Company said it had raised its stake in the Bulgarian-Greek telecom joint venture Bulfon to 34 percent from 32 percent. @
-- Bulgaria is expected to impose a 15 percent fee on grain exports, deputy trade minister Alexander Tasev said. At present exports are banned due to a grain shortage.
-- The Bulgarian State Railways said it may cut its passenger charges by 11 percent from July in a move to compete with road transport companies.
-- Bulgaria is expected to export 40,000 tonnes of steel to Spain this year under a bilateral cooperation agreement, Trade minister Valentin Vassilev said. @
-- Bulgaria's state National Television said it would cut 288 of its staff in line with government's policy to curb budget spending.

-- Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation accelerated to 5.6 percent in May from -0.7 percent in April mainly due to a sharp rise of vegetable, fruit and meat prices, the National Statistics Institute said.
-- Bulgarian exports to the European Union member countries amounted to $463 million in the first quarter of this year, deputy trade minister Hristo Mihailovski said. @
-- The Swiss firm Glencore won a third wheat import tender for 53,000 tonnes of bread wheat at $156.35 per tonne, deputy agriculture minister Valya Savcheva said.
-- Bulgaria posted $148.5 million trade deficit with Russia in the first quarter of this year, trade ministry figures showed.
-- The visiting Secretary General of the Atlantic Treaty Association Alfred Cahen said he supported Bulgaria's early admission into NATO to help promote stability in the Balkans.
